---
name: accessibility-and-plain-language-ui-101
description: "Build screens everyone can use: clear words, keyboard access, labels and contrast."
---
<!-- Generated by Pixl from the skill "Accessibility and plain-language UI", version 1. Edit it in the Skills tab, not here: changes made here are overwritten. -->

Plain language:
1. Use short everyday words; say what a button does ("Save changes", not "Submit"). One clear main action per screen.
2. Errors say what happened and what to do next, next to the field. Never show raw codes or stack traces.
3. Show empty, loading and error states for every list and every request.
Accessibility:
4. Use real HTML elements: `button`, `a`, `label`, `nav`, `main`, headings in order (h1 then h2). Not clickable divs.
5. Every input has a visible `<label for>`; every image has meaningful `alt` text (or empty alt if decorative).
6. Everything works with the keyboard alone: logical tab order, visible focus outline, Escape closes dialogs, no keyboard traps.
7. Contrast: text at least 4.5:1 against its background; never use color alone to show a state (add text or an icon).
8. Do not rely on hover; touch targets at least about 44 px; text can grow to 200 percent without breaking the layout.
9. Responsive layout: works on a phone width without sideways scrolling.
10. Announce changes: use `aria-live` for status messages, `aria-label` for icon-only buttons; do not add ARIA where a real element already does it.
11. Test: tab through the page, check labels in a component test, and mention what you could not check without a browser.
